t: 1. Manufacturing, Delivery and Document Lead Times
p: 1.1. The manufacturing lead time will be stated in the proposal in calendar days, counted from the fulfillment of the start conditions set forth in item 2 (Documentation and Payment Events), when applicable, or from receipt of the formal acceptance of the proposal, the purchase order and the down payment;

1.2. The delivery lead time corresponds to the number of calendar days required for transportation, and may be adjusted according to the destination, under the terms of the proposal. The count of the delivery lead time begins after the end of the manufacturing lead time.
1.3. Without prejudice to the specific lead times stated in the LS Fire Documentation Package, LS Fire will use its best efforts to begin making the basic technical documents available as follows:
– Pump Set: up to 20 (twenty) business days;
– Pump Skid: up to 30 (thirty) business days;
– Container / Pump House: up to 60 (sixty) business days;

counted from the date of receipt of the formal acceptance of the proposal, subject to the conditions precedent of item 2. In the event of any discrepancy between this indicative lead time and the specific lead times set out in the LS Fire Document Scope, the lead times of the Document Scope shall prevail for each document.

1.4. The detailed technical documentation will follow the LS Fire Technical Deliverables Index applicable to the supply, whose lead times are expressed in business days counted after receipt of the Purchase Order (DAPC) and, where an agreed down payment applies, also after the actual payment of such down payment, as detailed in said document.

1.5. The individual lead times of each deliverable, the quantity, the format and the information on whether or not it is included in the IOM Manual (Installation, Operation and Maintenance) are those set forth in the LS Fire Technical Deliverables Index in force at the time of the proposal, which becomes part of these General Terms and Conditions of Sale for the purpose of defining the documentation scope and lead times.

1.6. All documents will be provided in LS Fire standard PDF format (Dig.), unless otherwise specified. The IOM Manual will be provided in 1 (one) digital copy (Dig.) together with the Databook, unless specifically agreed otherwise in the proposal.
1.7. Documents will be delivered by e-mail or by electronic means indicated by the customer, subject to confirmation of the purchase order and, when applicable, to payment of the agreed down payment.

1.8. Changes requested by the customer to the scope, specifications, documents or drawings not provided for or not previously agreed in the proposal will only be implemented if technically feasible and accepted by LS Fire, and may result in a revision of the proposal, with price and lead time adjustment.

1.9. In the case of previously negotiated approval drawings, the drawing will be sent to the customer based on the scope defined and agreed in the proposal. If, upon reviewing the approval drawing, the customer requests another solution, configuration or feature that is not covered by the scope provided for and agreed, such request will be treated as a change of scope and may result in an extension of the lead time and additional costs, which will be assessed by LS Fire and communicated for the prior acceptance of the contracting party.
1.10. Specific reports and/or certificates not expressly mentioned in the proposal or in the LS Fire Document Scope are excluded from the scope of supply.
1.11. Unless expressly provided for in the commercial proposal or in the respective purchase order, the following are not included in the LS Fire scope of supply:
a) preparation and issue of drawings for prior approval (also referred to as "approval drawing", "for approval" or equivalent), before release for manufacturing;
b) participation in periodic technical meetings, in person or remote, for project follow-up, interface coordination or multidisciplinary validation;
c) project follow-up visits in the field or at the customer's facilities, for the purpose of inspection, supervision of third parties or construction management.
1.12. The items mentioned in subparagraphs "a", "b" and "c" above may be included in the scope upon express request by the customer and specific negotiation in the proposal, defining:
i) activities covered; ii) number of revisions, meetings and/or visits; iii) persons in charge and format (in person or remote); and iv) any impacts on lead time and price.

1.13. In the absence of a clear provision in the proposal or contract regarding approval drawings and/or follow-up meetings and visits, LS Fire shall only be obliged to issue and deliver the technical documents listed in the applicable LS Fire Document Scope and to provide the engineering services strictly necessary to fulfill the contracted supply.

1.14. Engineering drawings, including drawings for approval (“for approval”) and/or final drawings (“DTE - Detailed Technical Drawing”), are made available to the customer solely to enable the design, installation, operation and maintenance of the equipment and systems supplied, and do not mean the acquisition, by the customer, of the intellectual property over such drawings, which remains entirely with LS Fire, under the terms of clause 24.
– The individual lead times of each document are expressed in calendar days (DAPC, DART, DAE or ARDA), as detailed in the LS Fire Document Scope.
– "With IOM" indicates that the document is issued together with the Installation, Operation and Maintenance Manual.
– All technical drawings and documents are provided in 1 (one) electronic copy (Dig.).

2.1. When applicable, the proposal or contractual instrument will expressly state whether there are conditions precedent to the start of manufacturing or to invoicing, such as approval of the design by the customer, delivery of specific documentation or release of a payment installment.

2.2. The manufacturing lead time will only be counted from the full fulfillment of the agreed conditions precedent, and the period during which such conditions are pending due to an act or omission of the customer shall not constitute a delay by LS Fire.

2.3. Likewise, invoicing will only take place after fulfillment of the invoicing conditions that may be provided for in the proposal or contract, and the pending period shall not be deemed a default by LS Fire.

2.4. Any documentation or payment event that impacts the start of manufacturing or invoicing will be described objectively in the proposal, without indication of amounts or percentages in this clause.
2.5. Any delays in the preceding stages and payment events will impact the subsequent stages of the projects/services in the same proportion of time;
3.1. The freight modality (CIF, FOB or other) will be stated in the proposal.
3.2. FOB: collection shall take place at the LS Fire facility in Joinville/SC, with loading under the customer's responsibility.
3.3. CIF: the customer will be responsible for unloading at the destination and shall make the appropriate resources available for receipt.

3.3.1 The freight estimates presented by LS Fire are based on the conditions in force at the time of the proposal. Relevant and proven changes in logistics costs between the date of the proposal and the actual shipment of the equipment, arising, for example, from fuel price variations, adjustments to carriers' rate tables, regulatory changes, force majeure events, armed conflicts, traffic restrictions, unavailability of transportation or similar situations, may be passed on to the contracting party upon prior notice and presentation of the respective grounds.

t: 4. Imported Products and Changes in Inputs
p: 4.1. Imported items have an estimated invoicing forecast, subject to external factors such as sea freight, customs clearance, international availability and exchange rates. Delays arising from these conditions do not constitute a default by LS Fire.

4.2. Prices will remain fixed during the proposal validity period. If the US dollar exchange rate varies by more than 5% (five percent) between the date of the proposal and the date of invoicing, LS Fire may revise the prices of the affected imported items. The variation will be calculated based on the PTAX selling rate published by the Central Bank of Brazil (BACEN).

4.3. In the absence of a given input or in the event of a significant variation in price or lead time, LS Fire may replace it with another of similar quality, functionality and characteristics, upon notice to the customer, who will have 5 (five) days to state whether or not it agrees with the replacement, it being understood that silence shall imply agreement. The replacement will not compromise the product warranty.

5.1. The prices offered include labor costs for the commissioning and/or start-up services of the pump sets, including operational and hands-on training of the designated team, performed by an LS Fire authorized technician. This service covers 1 (one) day rate, valid for business days, during business hours (Monday to Friday, from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m., with a 1-hour lunch break).

5.2. Our technicians may provide service on Saturdays, Sundays, holidays and/or at night upon prior written request by the contracting party and express authorization by LS Fire, with the corresponding hours charged to the contracting party, in accordance with the labor legislation in force.

5.3. The service may be performed within up to 4 (four) months from the date of issue of the invoice for the set. During this period, the equipment must be preserved in accordance with the IOM Manual provided by LS Fire.
5.4. The technician's travel, lodging and meal expenses are the responsibility of LS Fire, within the period established in item 5.3.
5.5. Additional day rates must be previously authorized by LS Fire and will be charged at R$ 4.000,00 (four thousand reais) per day, plus additional expenses presented at the close of the service.

5.6. Scheduling must be requested from the LS Fire Service department, which will send the "Installation Checklist" form. The service will be scheduled within up to 15 (fifteen) business days after the completed form is returned, provided that the site is ready for testing.
5.7. Electrical, mechanical, hydraulic, civil installation or structural reinforcement services do not constitute technical delivery and are the sole responsibility of the contracting party.

6.1. Whether or not a penalty applies for late delivery by LS Fire to the customer will be expressly stated in the proposal or contractual instrument. In the absence of a specific provision, no penalty for late delivery shall apply.

6.2. When provided for, the late delivery penalty shall apply exclusively to delays attributable to LS Fire, and shall not apply to pending periods arising from events provided for in item 2 (Documentation and Payment Events), force majeure, acts of God, strikes, natural disasters, failures of international suppliers or any other factors beyond the control of LS Fire.
6.3. Late delivery does not authorize the contracting party to suspend or withhold payments of installments already due or falling due that are not related to the delayed item.

The applicable warranties vary according to the nature of the supply, subject to the conditions and exclusions below. To claim under the warranty, the Contracting Party shall contact LS Fire by e-mail describing the defect and attaching photos, videos and/or documents demonstrating the defect.

Considering the possibility of high complexity in resolving the defect presented under warranty, especially in the case of imported components, as well as the travel required to provide the warranty service, LS Fire will have a maximum period of 180 (one hundred and eighty) days to complete the repair and/or replacement of the defect presented, always using its best efforts to provide the warranty service in a shorter period, depending on the specific conditions of each case.
7.1. Equipment Warranty

7.1.1. The equipment supplied by LS Fire is warranted against defects in materials and workmanship for a period of 12 (twelve) months from the date of commissioning into operation (Start-up) or 18 (eighteen) months from the date of invoicing, whichever occurs first.

Considering the possibility of high complexity in resolving the defect presented under warranty, especially in the case of imported components, as well as the travel required to provide the warranty service, LS Fire will have a maximum period of 180 (one hundred and eighty) days to complete the repair and/or replacement of the defect presented, always using its best efforts to provide the warranty service in a shorter period, depending on the specific conditions of each case.

7.1.2. The warranty covers, at LS Fire's discretion, the repair or replacement of defective parts, at no material cost to the customer, excluding travel, transportation, disassembly, assembly and other indirect expenses, unless otherwise provided for in the proposal.
7.1.3. The warranty excludes damage arising from:
a) improper installation or installation not in accordance with the Operation and Maintenance Manual;
b) use under conditions other than those provided for in the design;
c) lack of preventive maintenance;
d) interventions by unauthorized third parties;
e) use of non-original parts or components;
f) force majeure events, casualties, flooding, fires, acts of vandalism or sabotage;
g) contamination of fluid (water, diesel oil or others) by solids, water, microorganisms or impurities beyond the limits acceptable to the manufacturer.
7.2. Services Warranty

7.2.1. Installation, assembly, commissioning, start-up, adjustment and maintenance services performed directly by LS Fire are warranted for 90 (ninety) days from completion of the services, limited to the correction of workmanship defects attributable to LS Fire.
7.2.2. The services warranty does not extend to failures arising from:
a) interference by third parties;
b) subsequent changes to the installation without LS Fire's consent;
c) operation of the system not in accordance with the Operation and Maintenance Manual;
d) lack of adequate preventive maintenance.
7.3. Payment Compliance Condition for Warranty

7.3.1. Entitlement to any warranty provided for in this instrument, whether relating to equipment, services, spare parts, technical assistance or technical support, is conditional upon the contracting party being up to date with its payments to LS Fire.

7.3.2. While there are liquid, overdue, undisputed and unpaid amounts after notice, the warranty will be automatically suspended, and LS Fire shall not be obliged to provide warranty service, free technical support, supply of parts under warranty or any other services covered by the warranty.

7.3.3. The suspension of the warranty due to non-payment shall not result in an extension of the originally established warranty periods, which will continue to run normally during the suspension period.

8.1. Field services comprise corrective and preventive maintenance, one-off inspections, pump house tests, alignments and assembly, performed at the contracting party's facilities by an LS Fire authorized technician.

8.2. The technician's travel, lodging and meal expenses are included in the price offered, valid for performance on a business day, during business hours (Monday to Friday, from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m., with a 1-hour lunch break), within the period established in the proposal.
8.3. Additional day rates must be previously authorized by LS Fire and will be charged at R$ 4.000,00 (four thousand reais) per day, plus extra expenses presented at the close of the service.

8.4. The contracting party shall ensure safe access to the site, provide minimum working conditions and, when necessary, provide a local helper. Inability to access the site on the scheduled day may give rise to the charging of an idle-time fee.
8.5. Scheduling must be requested from the Service department at least 15 (fifteen) business days in advance, except for duly justified emergencies.

9.1. Factory services comprise corrective and preventive maintenance performed at LS Fire's facilities, including disassembly, diagnosis, replacement of components, assembly and functional tests, according to the scope defined in the approved proposal or quotation.

9.2. Shipment of the equipment to the LS Fire factory is the responsibility of the contracting party, including freight, insurance and adequate packaging, unless otherwise provided for in the proposal or specific contract.

9.3. After the analysis, LS Fire will present a technical report and, when applicable, a quotation for repairs. Performance of the services will be subject to the prior approval of the contracting party.
9.4. In the case of an item under warranty, LS Fire will observe the conditions established in clause 7, bearing the costs of materials and repair services, within the limits set forth therein.

10.1. Engineering services may include, as contracted: feasibility studies, hydraulic sizing, equipment selection, preparation of calculation reports, technical drawings, descriptive reports, specifications and technical consulting.
10.2. The exact scope of the engineering services will be described in the proposal and/or in the LS Fire Document Scope, which becomes part of these General Terms and Conditions of Sale.

10.3. LS Fire's responsibility is limited to the disciplines and documents expressly mentioned in the proposal. Integration with other disciplines, overall project coordination or multidisciplinary compatibility checks will only be the responsibility of LS Fire if expressly provided for in the contractual instrument.
10.4. LS Fire is not responsible for changes of scope, design modifications or interferences introduced by third parties after delivery of the documents, unless a revision is contracted separately.

11.1. ITM contracts cover inspection, testing and maintenance of pumping systems and other related components, based on applicable standards, such as NFPA 25, as well as on manufacturers' recommendations and engineering best practices.
11.2. The exact scope of the ITM (frequency, items inspected, tests performed and maintenance covered) will be described in a specific proposal or in the service agreement.
11.3. Without prejudice to other items that may be included depending on the characteristics of the system, ITM services may cover:
a) visual inspections of pumps, panels, valves, piping and accessories;
b) automatic and manual start tests of the pump sets;
c) measurements of pressure, flow, electric current and other relevant parameters;
d) verification of alarms, interlocks and safety devices;
e) verification of fuel supply systems, tank levels, and integrity of lines and connections;
f) issue of technical reports recording non-conformities, corrective recommendations and photographic evidence;
g) technical guidance to the customer's team on operation and maintenance routines recommended by the manufacturer;
h) periodic tests in accordance with the frequency recommended by the standard (weekly, monthly, quarterly, annual), adjusted to the contracted scope;
i) issue of certificates or declarations of conformity for the tests performed, when applicable.
j) Ultimate Responsibility: In accordance with Section 4.1.1 of NFPA 25, the ultimate responsibility for the proper maintenance of the system remains with the owner.

11.4. Corrective services, emergency repairs or extraordinary inspections identified during the ITM and not included in the contracted scope will be quoted separately and performed only after approval by the contracting party.

11.5. LS Fire is not responsible for pre-existing deficiencies, systems inadequate for the current occupancy, or adverse conditions not reported by the contracting party that prevent the proper performance of the ITM.
11.6. Early cancellation subjects the contracting party to payment of a penalty proportional to the remaining period, as provided for in the contractual instrument.
11.7. Contracts will be renewed automatically at the end of the current term, unless otherwise notified in writing at least 30 (thirty) days in advance.

11.8. The contracting party acknowledges that LS Fire will reserve operational capacity, technical staff, structure and/or equipment to serve this inspection, testing and maintenance (ITM) contract. Therefore, regardless of the actual partial or full use of the services made available, the contracting party undertakes to pay the agreed minimum monthly, quarterly or annual amounts, constituting a take-or-pay obligation.

Non-use of the services, for reasons beyond LS Fire's control, shall not exempt the contracting party from paying the contracted amounts, considering the reservation of operational capacity, the technical availability and the commercial unavailability of the allocated resources.
12.1. The services cover activation, configuration, commissioning and remote or on-site technical support, according to the scope defined in the proposal.
12.2. The network, cabling and power infrastructure required for the operation of the FireConnect system is the sole responsibility of the contracting party.
12.3. Software updates and post-implementation remote support may be contracted separately under a specific support plan.

12.4. The warranty covers installation and configuration defects in work performed by LS Fire for a period of 90 (ninety) days from commissioning. Failures arising from changes to the network infrastructure or unauthorized interventions are not covered.

13.1. The supply of fuel tanks covers the equipment according to the specification in the proposal, excluding civil works, foundations, electrical installations and environmental licenses, which are the responsibility of the contracting party.

13.2. Diesel oil filtration systems are supplied according to the technical specification in the proposal. The filter replacement frequency must follow the recommendations of the Operation and Maintenance Manual provided by LS Fire.

14.1. The supply of pump command and control panels (SVE, Tornatech and equivalent) follows the technical specifications stated in the proposal, including, when applicable, UL/FM certifications and other regulatory requirements.

14.2. The electrical installation of the panel, including cabling, grounding and external protections, is the sole responsibility of the contracting party, unless expressly provided for in the proposal.

15.1. The rental of pumps, skids, containers, panels and complete systems is governed by a specific contractual instrument, which will define the rental period, the price, the delivery and return conditions, and the responsibilities of the parties.

15.2. During the rental period, the contracting party is responsible for the custody, preservation and proper operation of the equipment, in accordance with the Operation and Maintenance Manual provided by LS Fire.
15.3. Damage caused by improper use, negligence, unauthorized interventions or external events during the rental period is the sole responsibility of the contracting party.
15.4. The equipment shall be returned in the same condition as delivered, allowing for natural wear and tear. Additional damage identified upon return will be assessed and charged by LS Fire.

15.5. LS Fire is responsible for the preventive maintenance of the rented equipment, unless otherwise provided for in the contractual instrument. Corrective maintenance due to improper use will be charged separately.
15.6. Early cancellation subjects the contracting party to payment of the remaining installments or of a termination penalty, as provided for in the specific contractual instrument.

15.7. The contracting party acknowledges that LS Fire will reserve operational capacity, equipment and logistics structure to serve this rental contract. Accordingly, regardless of the actual full or partial use of the rented equipment, the contracting party undertakes to pay the agreed minimum monthly amount, constituting a take-or-pay obligation.

15.8. Partial or full non-use of the equipment or services made available by LS Fire during the rental period, when not arising from a failure attributable to LS Fire, shall not exempt the contracting party from the obligation to pay the contracted minimum amounts, considering the reservation of operational capacity, the technical availability and the commercial unavailability of the allocated resources.
16.1. Training covers operation, maintenance, application and products, delivered by an LS Fire authorized technician, according to the scope and workload defined in the proposal.

16.2. The technician's travel, lodging and meal expenses are included in the price offered, valid for performance on a business day, during business hours (Monday to Friday, from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m., with a 1-hour lunch break), within the period established in the proposal.

16.3. Services outside regular hours will depend on prior written request by the contracting party and express authorization by LS Fire, with the additional hours charged in accordance with the labor legislation in force.

17.1. The commercial terms are as stated in the proposal header, subject to credit analysis and approval by LS Fire, as well as to the prior submission of the documentation requested by the finance department.
17.2. Bank details for payment will not automatically be part of the commercial proposals.

After credit analysis and approval by the LS Fire finance department, the official bank details for invoicing and payment will be formally provided to the contracting party by means of the respective Bank Domicile Statement or equivalent document, which shall prevail for all financial and operational purposes.
LS Fire is not responsible for payments made to accounts other than those formally indicated in the Bank Domicile Statement in force or in communications not originating from its official channels.

17.3. In contracts with a term of 12 (twelve) months or longer, including, but not limited to, equipment rental, inspection, periodic testing and maintenance (ITM), monitoring, technical support and other recurring service contracts, the contracted amounts may be adjusted annually by the IPCA/IBGE accumulated over the period, or by another official index that may replace it.

17.3.1. The adjustment will be applied automatically every 12 (twelve) months counted from the date of signature of the contract, the issue of the purchase order or the base date defined in the commercial proposal, regardless of prior notice.
18.1. In the event of late payment, a late payment penalty of 2% on the amount due will apply, plus default interest of 1% per month pro rata die, in addition to monetary adjustment by the IPCA/IBGE.

18.2. The costs of out-of-court and judicial collection, including attorneys' fees in the amount of 20% of the amount of the debt, court costs, protests and administrative expenses, will be borne by the defaulting contracting party.

18.3. In the event of default on any installment for a period exceeding 15 (fifteen) calendar days, LS Fire may, at its sole discretion and regardless of prior notice, declare the acceleration of all installments falling due, making the entire outstanding balance immediately payable, plus the charges provided for in Clauses 18.1 and 18.2.

18.4. Service of process, summons and any official communication made by electronic means — including by e-mail, instant messaging application (WhatsApp, Telegram or similar) or Electronic Legal Domicile (DJe) — are fully valid and effective, dispensing with any form of personal service, pursuant to art. 246, §1 of the Code of Civil Procedure (CPC), and arts. 4 and 5 of Lei nº 14.063/2020.

18.5. In any legal action, service of process on the Contracting Party (legal entity) may be made through its respective Electronic Legal Domicile, as provided for in art. 246, §1 of the Code of Civil Procedure (CPC), with personal summons of its legal representatives being unnecessary.

Considering the efforts made by LS Fire to meet the established lead times, including, but not limited to, design, procurement, manufacturing and/or import of products, among others, in the event of cancellation, the following indemnity shall be owed to LS Fire, as reimbursement, to be paid in cash:
19.1. After the purchase order is sent: 10% of the total proposal amount.
19.2. Up to 20% of the manufacturing/execution lead time provided for in the contract: 20%.
19.3. Up to 40% of the manufacturing/execution lead time provided for in the contract: 40%.
19.4. Up to 60% of the manufacturing/execution lead time provided for in the contract: 60%.

20.1. LS Fire will retain ownership of the goods supplied until full payment of the agreed amounts. In the event of late payment, the company may request repossession of the products, applying a deduction of up to 50% of the total amount for depreciation, operating costs and any losses.
20.2. The delay will result in the acceleration of the remaining installments and may result in judicial collection of the outstanding amounts.

21.1. If the equipment is completed and ready for shipment and, for reasons attributable to the contracting party, cannot be delivered on the scheduled date, LS Fire may charge storage costs from the notice of readiness for shipment until the actual collection or delivery of the equipment.

21.2. Once 90 (ninety) days have elapsed from the notice of readiness without delivery having been made possible for reasons attributable to the contracting party, LS Fire may, at its sole discretion, cancel the order, applying the cancellation fees provided for in the corresponding clause.
22.1. The contracting party may request the temporary suspension of the order by written notice to LS Fire at least 5 (five) business days in advance, stating the expected suspension period.
22.2. Suspensions of up to 60 (sixty) days: LS Fire will inform the contracting party of any lead time and price adjustments arising from the reallocation of resources during the suspension period.

22.3. Suspensions exceeding 60 (sixty) days, consecutive or not: LS Fire may, at its sole discretion, treat the suspension as a cancellation, applying the fees provided for in the Order Cancellation clause.

22.4. LS Fire may suspend manufacturing, delivery of equipment, provision of services, technical assistance, commissioning, start-up, training and any other contractual obligations for as long as the contracting party is in default with LS Fire.
22.4.1. The suspension provided for in this clause shall not constitute a default by LS Fire, nor shall it entitle the contracting party to penalties, indemnities or compensation of any kind.

22.4.2. The lead times for manufacturing, delivery, supply of documents, performance of services and other obligations of LS Fire will be automatically extended by the period corresponding to the suspension, plus the time required to reschedule the activities.

23.1. The total liability of LS Fire to the contracting party, for any claim arising from the supply of equipment or services, shall in no event exceed the total amount of the order to which the claim refers.

23.2. Under no circumstances shall LS Fire be liable for indirect damages, loss of profits, loss of revenue, loss of use, consequential or punitive damages of any nature, even if it has been advised of the possibility of such damages.

23.3. LS Fire's liability will be proportionally reduced to the extent that the damages claimed arise from negligence, improper use or omission of the contracting party or of third parties contracted by it.

24.1. All technical drawings, designs, specifications, calculations, manuals, reports, software, catalogs and other technical documents prepared by LS Fire in connection with this supply constitute intellectual work owned exclusively by LS Fire, even if they have been made available to the contracting party.

24.2. Such documents are made available to the contracting party for the sole purpose of enabling the correct analysis, installation, operation and maintenance of the equipment and systems supplied, and in no event shall this imply a transfer of ownership or assignment of intellectual property rights over said materials.

24.3. The technical documents provided to the contracting party are intended exclusively for the use, operation and maintenance of the equipment and systems acquired, and their reproduction, adaptation, modification, assignment, sublicensing, disclosure to third parties or use for any other purpose not directly related to the object of this supply is prohibited, unless with the prior written authorization of LS Fire.

24.4. Reverse engineering, disassembly, copying, or partial or total reproduction of LS Fire's products, systems or technical documents with the aim of developing, on one's own account or through third parties, similar or competing solutions, designs or equipment is expressly prohibited.

t: 25. Preservation of Economic and Financial Balance
p: 25.1. The parties acknowledge that supervening and unforeseeable events, capable of causing a relevant economic impact, may occur during the term of the supply. In such case, the parties undertake to negotiate in good faith the revision of the contractual conditions, with a view to maintaining the economic and financial balance initially agreed.

25.2. The affected party shall notify the other party in writing of the occurrence. The parties shall meet within 15 (fifteen) calendar days after the notice to discuss the necessary adjustments, without such period constituting delay or default by either party.

25.3. Without prejudice to the provisions of item 4 (Imported Products and Changes in Inputs), it is acknowledged that part of LS Fire's production costs is subject to exchange rate variation, and it is impracticable to foresee its effects at the time of the proposal.
Variations of the US dollar exceeding 5% (five percent) in relation to the PTAX rate in force on the date of issue of the proposal may give rise to a price revision, as provided for in clause 4.2.

26.1. The parties undertake to fully comply with the applicable anti-corruption legislation, including Lei nº 12.846/2013 (Brazilian Anti-Corruption Law), Lei nº 8.429/1992 and other regulations in force, refraining from any act that constitutes corruption, bribery or undue favoring of public or private agents.
26.2. Neither party may offer, promise, give, authorize, request or accept any undue advantage, of any nature, whether directly or indirectly, in connection with this supply.
26.3. Should either party become aware of any act contrary to these provisions, it shall immediately notify the other party so that the appropriate measures may be taken.

27.1. Should any provision of this instrument be declared null, invalid or unenforceable by a judicial or arbitral decision, the remaining provisions shall remain in full force and effect, and the affected clause shall be deemed modified to the minimum extent necessary to make it valid, or deleted if such modification is not possible.
28.1. The courts of the District of Joinville/SC are hereby elected to settle any doubts or disputes arising from this instrument, with express waiver of any other, however privileged it may be.
